xxix
Technical Report of 26 th Indian Scientific Expedition
to Antarctica – An overview
Jayapaul D.
Expedition Leader and Station Commander
The National Center for Antarctic and Ocean Research which is India‘s
Premier Research Institute for Polar Science has progressed in leaps and bounds
in the formulation and implementation of the Scientific programmes of the
various organisations. There has been a complete reorientation of the scientific
programmes which is in tune with the requirements of the latest developments
in the field of Polar Science. I have been associated with the Indian Antarctic
Programme since the 16
th ISEA and have seen that a great deal of reorganization
has taken place in the past few years in the objectives of the scientific
programmes, developing state-of-art laboratory facilities and strategic new
logistic programmes to meet new requirements and challenges.
The National Center for Antarctic and Ocean Research has created awareness
among young Scientists and Research Scholars and has given an opportunity to
every participant scientist for advancing the frontiers of Antarctic Science by
providing all facilities and logistics of international standards. Climate change
and key related issues of Biodiversity and sustainability are the major issues
which mankind is facing today. There is an unprecedented surge in the awareness
the world over about climate change, biodiversity, degradation of natural
resources and energy. The National Center for Antarctic and Ocean Research
has clearly focused on these issues while formulating the Scientific Programmes.
The Technical Report of the XXVI Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica
pertains to the Scientific programmes and Logistic work carried out during the
Expedition by the participating organisations. The scientific papers have been
grouped under (a) Earth Sciences, Glaciology and Climate Change; (b)
Meteorology and Atmospheric Sciences; (c) Biology and Environmental Sciences;
(d) Engineering and Communication; (e) Medicine; and (f) Logistic Support.
ACHIEVEMENTS AND HIGHLIGHTS
Scientific (Summer)
Geological Survey of India team carried out ice core drilling in collaboration
with NCAOR. A total of 130 metres ice core was raised from the shelf.
Geological studies were carried out in Gruber and Zweissel mountains.
Glaciological studies included monitoring of Dakshin Gangotri Glacier snout
and western polar front of Schirmacher Oasis; Snow accumulation and ablation
studies on shelf; geological mapping in Larsemann Hills area and surrounding
islands.
xxx
National Geophysical Research Institute team carried out installation of a
new ASHTECH GPS; Regular downloading of the Broad band seismic data and
preliminary analysis of the data to identify earthquakes and regular downloading
of Turbo Rogue and ASHTECH GPS systems and Magnetotelluric studies to
delineate the deep crustal conductivity structure in Antarctica.
Indian Institute of Geomagnetism team carried out monitoring of geomagnetic
field intensity using Proton Precision Magnetometer; Ionospheric current system
using Fluxgate Magnetometer; Operation of GPS for studies on Glaciology and
Crustal Structure deformation Studies; Atmospheric vertical current and vertical
electrical field by long Wire antenna and Field Mill; and measurement of
Atmospheric Electrical Conductivity with Gerdien Condenser.
Indian Meteorological Department team carried out Brewer
Spectrophotometer observations for total Ozone; Three hourly weather
observations of atmospheric pressure, surface temperature, cloud cover surface
wind direction and surface wind speed; Hourly Microtop Atmospheric Turbidity
Aerosol Optical thickness observations; Continuous recording of AWS data and
Balloon ascents for Ozone Sonde observations.
Barkatullah University, Bhopal, Department of Limnology  Scientist carried
out studies on the Impact of Anthropogenic activities on flora and fauna of
Antarctic and high altitude Himalayan lakes of Ladakh.
Barkatullah University, Bhopal, Department of Physics Scientist carried out
studies on the space weather effect on navigation and communication.
National Center for Antarctic and Ocean Research team carried out study
of Polar microbes – linking diversity to ecosystem functioning and Geophysical
and Limnological studies of Antarctic lakes and their palaeoclimatic implications.
Snow and Avalanche Study Establishment team carried out Surface Energy
Balance study of the Antarctic ice sheet using AWS data.
Shriram Institute for Industrial Research team carried out long term
environment assessment of waste materials emanating over East Antarctica.
Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeobotany team carried out studies on the
Palaeoclimatic conditions in late Quaternary lakes of east Antarctica: A
multidisciplinary study using sedimentological, palynological, geochemical,
mineral, magnetic and chronological parameters.
